prompt_context_by_prefix.menu:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- libre software: ነጻ ሶፍትዌር
    DO NOT render as: free of charge, gratis, no-cost, or any price-sense rendering; phonetic transliteration of the English word "libre" as if it were a brand name; phonetic transliteration of "open source" where the language has its own term; wording that implies a free trial, a free tier, or a limited free version

menu.context: Software licensed so that its users are free to run, study, modify and redistribute it -- the freedom sense, never the price sense. Appears as the navbar item (menu_libre) and in the About page license section. Tom chose the English word "Libre" deliberately on 2026-08-09, over "Freely yours" and "Community software", citing LibreOffice as precedent.
menu.translation_notes: 2026-08-09 (Task 244): DEFER TO EACH LANGUAGE ESTABLISHED TERM, do not coin a new one. This concept has been translated by the free-software movement for decades and most of these languages have a settled, published phrase; ours must match it or it will read as an amateur calque. The English $ec_lang_syn entry deliberately offers coinages (Liberated / Liberty / Freedom Software) to convey the SENSE, because English lacks an unambiguous word -- that is an English-only problem and must NOT be exported. Where a language already distinguishes freedom from price (Romance libre/livre/libero/liber, de frei, ru свободное), use that word and the trap disappears. Where it does not, translate the concept (software whose users hold the rights) rather than transliterating "libre" phonetically -- transliteration is the specific failure mode this entry exists to prevent, and it falls hardest on am, bn, km, my, ps, ur.
